chunks: And as for what was narrated: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ali from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu Khalid, the mawla of Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the one who performs Umrah al-Mufradah, upon whom is the Tawaf al-Nisa', and he said: 'There is no Tawaf al-Nisa' upon him.'

So it is not contradictory to what we have previously mentioned, because this report is understood to mean that when a person enters in a state of Umrah al-Mufradah during the months of Hajj, then wishes to convert it into Umrat al-Tamattu' for Hajj, this is permissible for him, and Tawaf al-Nisa' does not become obligatory upon him, because Tawaf al-Nisa' is only obligatory upon the one who performs Umrah and does not combine it with Hajj (Tamattu'). So when he combines it with Hajj, its obligation is lifted from him.

And that which indicates this is what was narrated: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn Isa, who said: Abu al-Qasim Mukhallad ibn Musa al-Razi wrote to the Imam (peace be upon him), asking him about Umrah al-Mubtulah (Umrah performed alone without combining with Hajj), whether Tawaf al-Nisa' is upon its owner, and about the Umrah that is combined with Hajj (Umrat al-Tamattu'), so he wrote: 'As for Umrah al-Mubtulah, Tawaf al-Nisa' is upon its owner; and as for the one that is combined with Hajj, Tawaf al-Nisa' is not upon its owner.'

key_terms.طَوَافُ النِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-Nisa', an additional circumambulation performed by women after the main Tawaf
key_terms.عُمْرَةٌ مُفْرَدَةٌ: Umrah performed independently, not combined with Hajj
key_terms.عُمْرَةُ الْمَبْتُولَةِ: Umrah performed alone (literally 'the separated/alone Umrah'), referring to Umrah al-Mufradah
key_terms.يَتَمَتَّعُ بِهَا إِلَى الْحَجِّ: To combine it with Hajj, referring to Umrat al-Tamattu'

ai.seo_question: Is Tawaf al-Nisa' obligatory for Umrat al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi utilizes this narration to resolve the apparent contradiction regarding the obligation of Tawaf al-Nisa' by distinguishing between the independent Umrah (Mufradah), which retains the obligation, and the Umrah combined with Hajj (Tamattu'), where it is lifted. This interpretation aligns with the principle that the specific ritual of Umrat al-Tamattu' serves as a complete substitute, thereby exempting the pilgrim from the additional burden of the women's circumambulation.
